protocol: MQTT 3.1.1 (OASIS, protocol level 0x04) over TCP — CONNECT / CONNACK / SUBSCRIBE / SUBACK, plus PINGREQ / PINGRESP for keepalive liveness

captures.label: CONNECT (client → broker) — will flag set, username+password set, remaining length in 2-byte varint form
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:fixedHeader:0x10 — packetType=1 (CONNECT), flags nibble=0b0000 (reserved, MUST be 0)
1:2:remainingLength:8f 01 — 7-bit continuation varint, value=143 = byte count of offsets 3..145. TWO bytes because 143>=128: 143%128=15 -> 15|0x80=0x8f, 143/128=1 -> 0x01
3:2:protocolNameLen:00 04 — u16be = 4
5:4:protocolName:4d 51 54 54 — "MQTT"
9:1:protocolLevel:04 — MQTT 3.1.1
10:1:connectFlags:0xce — b7 userNameFlag=1; b6 passwordFlag=1; b5 willRetain=0; b4..b3 willQoS=0b01 (=1); b2 willFlag=1; b1 cleanSession=1; b0 reserved=0. THIS BYTE GATES OFFSETS 32..145
11:2:keepAliveSeconds:00 3c — u16be = 60
13:2:clientIdLen:00 11 — u16be = 17
15:17:clientId:6e 65 78 61 66 6c 6f 77 2d 70 72 6f 62 65 2d 30 31 — "nexaflow-probe-01"
32:2:willTopicLen:00 0a — u16be = 10. PRESENT ONLY BECAUSE connectFlags.b2 == 1
34:10:willTopic:64 65 76 2f 73 74 61 74 75 73 — "dev/status". PRESENT ONLY BECAUSE connectFlags.b2 == 1
44:2:willMessageLen:00 50 — u16be = 80. PRESENT ONLY BECAUSE connectFlags.b2 == 1
46:80:willMessage:7b 22 73 74 61 74 75 73 22 3a 22 6f 66 66 6c 69 6e 65 22 2c 22 72 65 61 73 6f 6e 22 3a 22 75 6e 67 72 61 63 65 66 75 6c 2d 64 69 73 63 6f 6e 6e 65 63 74 22 2c 22 6e 6f 64 65 22 3a 22 6e 65 78 61 66 6c 6f 77 2d 70 72 6f 62 65 2d 30 31 22 7d — 80 bytes, exactly '{"status":"offline","reason":"ungraceful-disconnect","node":"nexaflow-probe-01"}'. MQTT defines no internal structure for this field — it is an opaque application payload, so these 80 bytes ARE the field. PRESENT ONLY BECAUSE connectFlags.b2 == 1
126:2:usernameLen:00 0a — u16be = 10. PRESENT ONLY BECAUSE connectFlags.b7 == 1
128:10:username:73 65 6e 73 6f 72 75 73 65 72 — "sensoruser". PRESENT ONLY BECAUSE connectFlags.b7 == 1

[TOTAL 146 bytes, offsets 0..145. Declared remainingLength 143 == actual 146-3 = 143. VERIFIED.]
captures.notes: Chosen legal values (not from a real capture, all spec-legal): clientId "nexaflow-probe-01", keepAlive 60s, will topic "dev/status", credentials sensoruser/s3cr3t. The will payload was deliberately sized to 80 bytes to push remainingLength to 143 and force the TWO-byte varint form — a 1-byte-varint capture would have hidden the grammar's central failure.

captures.label: CONNACK (broker → client) — connection accepted, no session resumed
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:fixedHeader:0x20 — packetType=2 (CONNACK), flags nibble=0b0000 (reserved, MUST be 0)
1:1:remainingLength:02 — varint, ONE-byte form because 2<128, value=2 = byte count of offsets 2..3
2:1:connectAcknowledgeFlags:0x00 — b7..b1 reserved=0000000; b0 sessionPresent=0. MUST be 0 here because the CONNECT set cleanSession=1
3:1:connectReturnCode:0x00 — 0x00 = Connection Accepted (0x01 unacceptable protocol version, 0x02 identifier rejected, 0x03 server unavailable, 0x04 bad user/password, 0x05 not authorized)
[TOTAL 4 bytes, offsets 0..3. Declared remainingLength 2 == actual 4-2 = 2. VERIFIED.]
captures.notes: Same protocol, ONE-byte varint. The two captures together prove the width of the length field is a function of its own value.

captures.label: SUBSCRIBE (client → broker) — three topic filters at QoS 1, 2, 0
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:fixedHeader:0x82 — packetType=8 (SUBSCRIBE), flags nibble=0b0010. This nibble is NOT free: MQTT mandates exactly 0010; any other value is a protocol error the server must answer by closing the connection
1:1:remainingLength:36 — varint, ONE-byte form, value=54 = byte count of offsets 2..55
2:2:packetIdentifier:00 0a — u16be = 10. MUST be non-zero; correlation token echoed by SUBACK
4:2:topicFilterLen[0]:00 0a — u16be = 10
6:10:topicFilter[0]:64 65 76 2f 73 74 61 74 75 73 — "dev/status"
16:1:requestedQoS[0]:01 — QoS 1; upper 6 bits reserved, MUST be 0
17:2:topicFilterLen[1]:00 0f — u16be = 15
19:15:topicFilter[1]:64 65 76 2f 2b 2f 74 65 6c 65 6d 65 74 72 79 — "dev/+/telemetry" (single-level wildcard)
34:1:requestedQoS[1]:02 — QoS 2
35:2:topicFilterLen[2]:00 12 — u16be = 18
37:18:topicFilter[2]:24 53 59 53 2f 62 72 6f 6b 65 72 2f 75 70 74 69 6d 65 — "$SYS/broker/uptime"
55:1:requestedQoS[2]:00 — QoS 0
[TOTAL 56 bytes, offsets 0..55. Declared remainingLength 54 == actual 56-2 = 54. VERIFIED.]
captures.notes: The payload is a repeated (u16be length, bytes, u8 qos) record — a length prefix INSIDE a repetition, with a trailing scalar after the variable-length part. Not a TLV: the tag-equivalent (QoS) comes last.

captures.label: SUBACK (broker → client) — one exact grant, one DOWNGRADE, one failure
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:fixedHeader:0x90 — packetType=9 (SUBACK), flags nibble=0b0000
1:1:remainingLength:05 — varint, ONE-byte form, value=5 = byte count of offsets 2..6
2:2:packetIdentifier:00 0a — u16be = 10, echoes the SUBSCRIBE at capture 3
4:1:returnCode[0]:01 — Success, maximum QoS 1. Requested 1 -> granted 1. EXACT
5:1:returnCode[1]:01 — Success, maximum QoS 1. Requested 2 -> granted 1. NEGOTIATED DOWNGRADE: the broker's max-qos policy narrowed the request; the client must now treat this subscription as at-most-once-duplicated, not exactly-once
6:1:returnCode[2]:80 — 0x80 = Failure. Requested 0 -> NOT GRANTED AT ALL. "$SYS/broker/uptime" is refused by ACL; no subscription exists. The client learns this only here, and any later absence of data on that topic is expected, not a fault
[TOTAL 7 bytes, offsets 0..6. Declared remainingLength 5 == actual 7-2 = 5. VERIFIED.]
captures.notes: Return-code count is positionally bound to the SUBSCRIBE's filter count — there is no count field. The decoder derives it as remainingLength-2, i.e. from a value it can only obtain by correctly decoding the varint.

captures.label: PINGREQ (client → broker) — keepalive liveness probe
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:fixedHeader:0xc0 — packetType=12 (PINGREQ), flags nibble=0b0000
1:1:remainingLength:00 — varint, ONE-byte form, value=0; no variable header, no payload
[TOTAL 2 bytes, offsets 0..1. Declared remainingLength 0 == actual 2-2 = 0. VERIFIED.]
captures.notes: Included because the assigned hazard names keepalive liveness. This is the only message whose obligation is periodic rather than event-driven.

captures.label: PINGRESP (broker → client) — liveness confirmation
captures.fieldBreakdown:
0:1:fixedHeader:0xd0 — packetType=13 (PINGRESP), flags nibble=0b0000
1:1:remainingLength:00 — varint, ONE-byte form, value=0
[TOTAL 2 bytes, offsets 0..1. Declared remainingLength 0 == actual 2-2 = 0. VERIFIED.]
captures.notes: Confirms the broker was alive at receipt. That confirmation decays immediately — it is a TTL fact, not a durable state.

statefulness:
MQTT is not a request/response protocol with a state machine bolted on; the connection IS the state, and §5 is missing most of what it needs.

LEGAL-MESSAGE-PER-STATE. The real state set is larger than "disconnected/connected". (1) tcpClosed — nothing legal. (2) tcpOpen — TCP is up, CONNECT has not been sent. EXACTLY ONE message is legal: CONNECT. The broker must close the socket if the first packet is anything else. (3) connectSent — CONNECT is on the wire, CONNACK has not arrived. NOTHING is legal here, not even a second CONNECT. §5 cannot name this state: it is neither disconnected nor connected, it is in-flight, and v0's transitions are edge-triggered on completion, so the pending interval has no name and therefore no validIn can exclude it. (4) connected — SUBSCRIBE / UNSUBSCRIBE / PUBLISH / PINGREQ / DISCONNECT. (5) rejected — CONNACK returnCode != 0; terminal, broker closes; the client must send nothing further. Different codes imply different remediation (0x04 bad credentials -> reprompt; 0x02 identifier rejected -> regenerate clientId; 0x03 server unavailable -> backoff) so this is really five terminal sub-states, which v0 CAN express as multiple `transitions` with `when` guards. That part works.

WHAT MUST CHAIN. SUBSCRIBE requires a CONNECT that was ACCEPTED, in the SAME TCP connection. §5's `requires:["login"]` has no declared scope — run, session, or store. It must be session-scoped and must be invalidated the instant the socket closes, otherwise a reconnect silently inherits a satisfied `requires` and the grammar authorises an illegal SUBSCRIBE on a fresh, un-CONNECTed socket. This is a specification hole, not a syntax hole.

WHAT MUST NEVER COMBINE. Not message-vs-message (`conflicts` handles that shape) but FIELD-vs-FIELD inside one message, which §5 cannot reach at all: passwordFlag=1 with userNameFlag=0; willFlag=0 with willQoS!=0 or willRetain=1; reserved bit0 != 0; packetIdentifier == 0; SUBSCRIBE fixed-header low nibble != 0b0010. Also cross-message: cleanSession=1 in CONNECT with sessionPresent=1 in CONNACK is a broker violation the client must detect. And self-occurrence: CONNECT is legal AT MOST ONCE per connection — `conflicts` is pairwise across different messages and cannot say "not twice".

CONFIRMED vs PRESUMED. CONNACK returnCode==0x00 CONFIRMS `connected` — this is the clean case and v0 handles it. Everything else is murkier. SUBSCRIBE presumes a subscription at the REQUESTED QoS; SUBACK then confirms it at a POSSIBLY LOWER one, or refuses it entirely with 0x80. So the confirmation does not validate the presumption, it OVERWRITES it with a narrower value — element by element, positionally. §5's `effects.presume` writes one fact from one expression and `confirmedBy.matches` is a whole-message boolean; neither can express "the response rewrites my presumption downward, per array element". Its own known-gaps list names this ("negotiated capability") and my capture confirms it: SUBACK 01 01 80 against a request of 1/2/0 cannot be recorded. PINGRESP confirms liveness only AT THE INSTANT OF RECEIPT — it is the purest TTL fact in the protocol (confidence high, ttl = keepAlive), and it decays to presumed immediately. The subscription set after a reconnect with sessionPresent=1 is state RESTORED from the broker's memory that this run never observed being created — neither confirmed nor presumed but asserted-by-the-peer, a third category §5 has no word for.

KEEPALIVE IS AN OBLIGATION, NOT A TIMEOUT. §5 offers `"connected": {"timeoutMs":30000,"onTimeout":"disconnected"}` — that models THE PEER going quiet. MQTT inverts it: WE must transmit something every KeepAlive seconds or the broker disconnects us at 1.5x KeepAlive. There is no periodic-emission primitive; the closest v0 construct is `delay` plus a back edge carrying `loop:{max:n}` with n <= 64, which caps a session at 64 heartbeats — a 60-second keepalive gives you a 64-minute maximum session lifetime as a hard grammar limit. Worse, `timeoutMs` is shown as a literal, but the correct value is `inputs.keepAliveSeconds * 1500` — negotiated by our own CONNECT field.

DISCOVERED ONLY FROM THE NEXT RESPONSE — OR FROM NO RESPONSE AT ALL. This is where §5's `implies` construct breaks. Its example keys on decoded content (`capture.status == 401`). MQTT's session-death signals mostly have NO content: (a) half-open TCP — you learn the session is dead when a PINGREQ produces no PINGRESP, i.e. from an ABSENCE, and there is no `capture.*` to test; (b) SESSION TAKEOVER — another client connects with your clientId and the broker disconnects you with no MQTT-level message whatsoever, just a FIN; (c) a QoS-2 downgrade to QoS 1 is NEVER reported again after the SUBACK — you do not discover a mismatch, deliveries just silently duplicate, which is a semantic divergence no response ever surfaces; (d) a 0x80 return code means the topic subscription does not exist, so the eternal absence of messages on that topic is CORRECT behaviour — indistinguishable at the transport level from a broker that has nothing to publish. So `implies` must be able to fire on `on:"timeout"` / `on:"error"` / `on:"close"` edges, not only on a decoded `when`.

ONE MORE STRUCTURAL DEMAND. MQTT is bidirectional-asynchronous over ONE socket: the broker sends PUBLISH unprompted at any moment, freely interleaved with the SUBACK you are waiting for, and freely coalesced into the same TCP segment. §4's `expect` with `token` correlation presumes a request/response run; here it must first FRAME every arriving packet (impossible — see the framing gap), CLASSIFY it, dispatch PUBLISH to a concurrent handler, and only then match the packet identifier. There is no always-on inbound channel in the step graph; `listen` is a step you arrive at, not a handler that runs alongside. Any MQTT client built on v0 would lose every PUBLISH that arrives while a step is waiting.

FINALLY, THE WILL. The will message is published by the broker if and only if the connection ends WITHOUT a DISCONNECT. That is a remote side effect determined by HOW a state was exited — the one piece of protocol state whose outcome depends on the exit path rather than on any message sent. §5 has no vocabulary for it: `effects` attach to a message succeeding, and abnormal termination is precisely the case where no message was sent.

gaps.what: No variable-width integer field. MQTT's Remaining Length is a 1-4 byte base-128 varint with a continuation bit, whose WIDTH is a function of the VALUE it carries.
gaps.why: CONNECT offset 1: `8f 01` = 143. CONNACK offset 1: `02` = 2. Same field, different widths, same protocol. §3's two-pass rule states pass 1 emits "a placeholder of the DECLARED WIDTH" and pass 2 back-patches — but the width here is only knowable after the span it measures is encoded, which is pass-2 knowledge. Reserving 4 bytes always is not an option: MQTT declares non-minimal encodings malformed. The v0 workaround (three mutually-exclusive u8 fields gated by `when` on `len(group:rest)`) makes field PRESENCE depend on a forward span, which the two-pass contract does not support at all — pass 1 fixes presence, pass 2 fixes only values.

gaps.what: No field that reads N bytes where N is a previously-decoded value. Every MQTT string is u16be-length + N bytes.
gaps.why: CONNECT offsets 13-15: read `00 11` = 17, then read 17 bytes as UTF-8. The decode grammar offers fixed-width scalars, `skip:<const>` (which discards), `bits`, and `each:<count>`. The nearest cheat, { "each":"capture.clientIdLen", "fields":[{"u8":null}], "as":"clientIdBytes" }, yields List<Int> not Text, and `each` has no post-conversion slot so `| concat | utf8` cannot be applied. Recovering the string requires a §4 `compute` step outside the parse document. This defeats EVERY string in CONNECT (protocolName, clientId, willTopic, willMessage, username, password) and every topic filter in SUBSCRIBE — 6 of 8 variable fields in the capture.

gaps.what: No stream frame kind can delimit an MQTT packet on TCP.
gaps.why: §2 offers exactly four: lengthPrefixed{prefix,at,includesPrefix} requires a FIXED-width prefix at a FIXED offset — MQTT's prefix is a 1-4 byte varint at offset 1 that excludes both itself and the header byte; delimited needs a byte sequence that cannot occur in a binary payload; fixed is wrong by construction; none leaves the stream unframed. Concretely: a broker may return `90 05 00 0a 01 01 80` (SUBACK) and a PUBLISH in ONE TCP segment, and may split my 146-byte CONNECT across two. With frame:none, `expect` has no packet boundary and cannot know where SUBACK ends.
gaps.proposedFix:
"frame": { "kind":"varintPrefixed", "at":1, "encoding":"mqtt7", "includesPrefix":false, "includesHeader":false, "headerBytes":1 }
A fifth frame kind, parameterised — it also covers Protobuf-delimited streams, LEB128 framing, and MQTT 5. Smaller than an `mqtt` layer and not protocol-specific.

gaps.what: `each` cannot contain a per-item length prefix, because group names have no iteration scoping.
gaps.why: SUBSCRIBE payload at offsets 4..55 is 3 x (u16be len, topic bytes, u8 qos). The natural form is {"each":"inputs.subscriptions","as":"r","fields":[{"u16be":"len(group:t)"},{"group":"t","fields":[{"value":"r.topic|utf8"}]},{"u8":"r.qos"}]}. §3 defines `len(group:X)` as a document-global span reference and says nothing about iteration scoping, so on iteration 2 `group:t` is either iteration 1's span or an ambiguous/cyclic reference — and §3 says cyclic span dependency is a VALIDATION error, so this document may not even load. I had to hand-unroll to exactly three topics, producing a document that encodes THIS SUBSCRIBE rather than SUBSCRIBE. Note the diagnostic contrast: SUBACK's `each` over bare u8 return codes works fine — the failure is localised precisely to the length-prefix-inside-repetition construct. `tlvList` does not help: MQTT's record is length-value-TAG (QoS trails the value), not tag-length-value.

gaps.what: `each` has no end-of-container termination form; the count must be a number.
gaps.why: SUBSCRIBE offsets 4..55 contain "as many (len,topic,qos) records as fit in remainingLength" — the count is nowhere in the packet. §3's decode `each` takes a count expression ("capture.byteCount / 2"). Deriving it here is impossible: the records are variable-length, so record count is not a function of byte count. SUBACK escapes only because its records are 1 byte each, letting me write `capture.remainingLength - 2` — and even that is dead while gap 1 stands.
gaps.proposedFix:
{ "each": "untilEnd", "as":"subscriptions", "fields":[ ... ] }  // repeat until the enclosing frame/group is exhausted; a partial trailing record is a decode error
Also accept "untilEnd(group:rest)" to bound it to a named span rather than the frame.

gaps.what: No bitwise operators in the expression language.
gaps.why: Reconstructing Remaining Length needs (rl0 & 0x7f) | ((rl1 & 0x7f) << 7) | ... — for CONNECT's `8f 01` that is (0x8f & 0x7f) + (0x01 & 0x7f)*128 = 15 + 128 = 143. §6's converter table is explicitly a CLOSED set and contains no and/or/shl/shr/bit; `xor(k)` is in the bytes group and operates on Bytes, not Int. Testing the will-flag from a captured byte (connectFlags & 0x04 at offset 10) hits the same wall. There is literally no expression in v0 that computes the value of the field the whole protocol is framed by.
gaps.proposedFix: Add to the numeric group: and(k) or(k) shl(n) shr(n) bit(n) — e.g. "capture.connectFlags | bit(2)" -> Int 0|1, and "capture.rl0 | and(0x7f)". Smallest possible fix, generalises to every bitfield protocol. (Partly mooted for Remaining Length once the varint fieldKind lands, but `bit(n)` is still needed for any guard over an already-captured byte.)

gaps.what: Decode-mode `when` is unspecified, and specifying it commits the decoder to being a stateful left-to-right fold.
gaps.why: CONNECT offsets 32..125 exist ONLY because bit 2 of the byte at offset 10 is set. Offsets 126..137 only because bit 7 is. Offsets 138..145 only because bit 6 is. That is 114 of 146 bytes — 78% of the packet — whose PRESENCE is decided by a byte read 22 bytes earlier. §3's decode example shows only `as`, `skip` and `each`; `when` never appears in decode mode. And §5's own known-gaps list still has "No decoder-carried state ... decode is not a pure per-field fold" OPEN, so the spec is on record as not having committed to this.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify: the decoder is a left-to-right fold over an incrementally-populated `capture` scope. `when` and `each` count expressions may reference any capture bound STRICTLY EARLIER in the same field list. Forward references are a VALIDATE-time error (statically checkable by index). No new syntax — a semantic guarantee that also settles CoAP option deltas and every other accumulating decoder in the known-gaps list.

gaps.what: Decode-mode `bits` with per-sub-field `as` is not specified.
gaps.why: The connect-flags byte at offset 10 (0xce) must decode into six named captures of widths 1,1,1,2,1,1,1 for `when` guards to reference. §3 shows `bits` only in ENCODE form with `value`. Without it the only route is {"u8":null,"as":"connectFlags"} plus bitwise tests, which gap 6 forbids — so gaps 6 and 7 are mutually load-bearing and at least one MUST be fixed.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify the decode dual: { "bits":[ {"n":1,"as":"userNameFlag"}, {"n":1,"as":"passwordFlag"}, {"n":1,"as":"willRetain"}, {"n":2,"as":"willQos"}, {"n":1,"as":"willFlag"}, {"n":1,"as":"cleanSession"}, {"n":1,"as":"reservedBit"} ] } — exactly mirroring the encode form, each entry producing an Int.

gaps.what: Non-minimal varint encodings make encode(decode(bytes)) provably lossy, and nothing can reject them.
gaps.why: The bytes `8f 80 00` are a legal-looking continuation chain decoding to 15 + 0*128 + 0*16384 = 15. Re-encoding 15 minimally yields `0f` — one byte, not three. So encode(decode(b)) != b. MQTT declares such an encoding malformed, but v0 can neither reject it on decode (no validation hook) nor preserve it on re-encode (no width memory). This is the single point where round-trip is not merely unimplemented but IMPOSSIBLE to make total without a new construct.
gaps.proposedFix: The varint fieldKind from gap 1 carries "minimal": true, meaning: on decode, a continuation chain that is not the shortest representation of its value is a DECODE ERROR, not a value. That makes the value->bytes map injective and restores encode(decode(b)) == b by construction. The alternative — capturing the observed width as a shadow capture and replaying it — should be REJECTED: it preserves malformed input rather than rejecting it.

gaps.what: No composite/record input type; `each ... as:"r"` binds a scalar.
gaps.why: SUBSCRIBE needs list<{topic:text, qos:u8}> — offsets 4..16, 17..34, 35..55 are three (string,byte) pairs. §6's injectable `type` set is text|int|u8..u64|bytes|hex|mac|ipv4|ipv6|port|bool|enum|secret|list<T> with T scalar, and §3's example {"each":"inputs.registers","as":"r","fields":[{"u16be":"r"}]} uses r as a bare scalar. There is no r.topic / r.qos. Combined with gap 4 this is what forced hand-unrolling.
gaps.proposedFix:
Add a record shape to inputs and member access to the `each` binding:
{ "name":"subscriptions", "kind":"prompt", "type":"list<record>",
  "shape": { "topic":"text", "qos":"u8" },
  "description":"Topic filters and the QoS to request for each" }
then "r.topic" / "r.qos" resolve as paths. Decode dual: `each ... as:"subscriptions"` with named `as` on inner fields produces a List<record>.

gaps.what: No negotiated-capability primitive: a response that grants LESS than requested, per element.
gaps.why: SUBACK offsets 4,5,6 = 01 01 80 against a SUBSCRIBE requesting 1,2,0. Element 1 exact; element 2 DOWNGRADED 2->1; element 3 REFUSED (0x80 means no subscription exists at all). §5's `effects.presume` writes ONE fact path from ONE expression, and `confirmedBy.matches` is a whole-message boolean ("capture.state == inputs.state") which would be FALSE here and merely mark the operation failed — losing the fact that two of three subscriptions succeeded at a narrowed capability. §5 lists this as a known gap; the capture confirms it is real and blocking for any correct MQTT client.
gaps.proposedFix:
"confirmedBy": { "message":"mqttSuback", "correlate":"packetId" },
"negotiates": {
  "requested": "inputs.subscriptions",
  "granted":   "capture.grantedCodes",
  "zip":       "index",
  "reject":    "granted == 0x80",
  "assert":    "granted <= requested.qos",
  "as":        "session.subscriptions[requested.topic].grantedQos" }
Rejected elements are recorded as absent, not as failures. `assert` catches a broker granting MORE than asked, which is a protocol violation.

gaps.what: No always-on inbound channel; the step graph cannot receive unsolicited messages.
gaps.why: MQTT is bidirectional-asynchronous over one socket. Between my SUBSCRIBE and its SUBACK the broker may emit any number of PUBLISH packets, possibly in the SAME TCP segment as the SUBACK. §4's `expect` with `token` correlation presumes request/response; `listen` is a step you arrive at, not a concurrent handler. Any client built on v0 discards every PUBLISH that arrives while a step is waiting — which for MQTT means discarding the entire point of the protocol.
gaps.proposedFix:
Declare inbound dispatch on the connection alongside `frame`:
"inbound": [ { "match":"packetType >> 4 == 3", "parse":"mqttPublish", "to":"onPublish" },
             { "match":"packetType >> 4 == 13", "parse":"mqttPingresp", "to":"onPingresp" } ]
and specify `expect` as DEMULTIPLEXING: it frames and classifies every arriving packet, routes non-matching ones to `inbound`, and returns only on a token match or timeout.

gaps.what: Keepalive is a transmission OBLIGATION, not a peer timeout, and periodic emission is inexpressible.
gaps.why: CONNECT offset 11-12 = `00 3c` (60s). MQTT requires the CLIENT to transmit something within every 60s window or the broker disconnects at 90s. §5 offers only "connected":{"timeoutMs":30000,"onTimeout":"disconnected"} — which models the PEER going quiet, the inverse relationship. The only v0 route is `delay` plus a back edge carrying loop:{max:n} with n<=64 (§4), which imposes a HARD GRAMMAR LIMIT of 64 heartbeats — a 64-minute maximum session at this keepalive. `timeoutMs` is also a literal where the correct value is a function of a field we ourselves sent.

gaps.what: `implies` fires only on decoded response content; MQTT's state-death signals have no content.
gaps.why: §5's example keys on "capture.status == 401". MQTT session death is observed as: (a) a PINGREQ producing no PINGRESP — an ABSENCE, no capture exists to test; (b) session takeover by another client using the same clientId — the broker sends a bare TCP FIN, zero MQTT bytes; (c) a QoS downgrade that is never re-reported, so deliveries silently duplicate forever with no error at any layer. Cases (a) and (b) are the two most common real failures and neither produces a `capture.*`.
gaps.proposedFix:
Allow `implies` entries keyed on the edge rather than on content:
"implies": [ { "on":"timeout", "state":"tcpClosed", "invalidate":["session.subscriptions","session.connected"] },
             { "on":"close",   "state":"tcpClosed", "invalidate":["session.*"] },
             { "when":"capture.connectReturnCode == 5", "state":"rejected", "invalidate":["store.credentials"] } ]
i.e. `implies` accepts `on` (edge) OR `when` (content), same as §4 edges already do.

gaps.what: No cross-field invariants; illegal packets encode happily.
gaps.why: MQTT mandates several combinations that v0 cannot forbid: passwordFlag=1 requires userNameFlag=1 (connectFlags 0x4a is illegal but encodes fine); willFlag=0 requires willQoS=0 AND willRetain=0; reserved bit 0 must be 0; packetIdentifier must be non-zero (offset 2-3 of SUBSCRIBE); SUBSCRIBE's fixed-header low nibble must be exactly 0b0010 (offset 0 = 0x82, not 0x80). A grammar that emits provably-invalid packets is worse than one that refuses them.
gaps.proposedFix:
Per-message "invariants": a list of boolean expressions, checked at VALIDATE time against constant inputs and at encode time against runtime ones, and asserted on decode:
"invariants": [ "inputs.hasPassword == 0 || inputs.hasUsername == 1",
                "inputs.willFlag == 1 || (inputs.willQos == 0 && inputs.willRetain == 0)",
                "inputs.packetId != 0" ]

gaps.what: `seq.next` cannot express the MQTT packet-identifier space.
gaps.why: SUBSCRIBE offset 2-3 = `00 0a`. The identifier must be u16, NON-ZERO, wrap 1..65535, be unique among IN-FLIGHT messages only, and be released when the SUBACK at offset 2-3 echoes it back. §6 gives `seq.next` as a bare persisted monotonic counter — no width, no minimum, no wrap, no release.

gaps.what: No way to model state RESTORED by a peer assertion rather than created by this run.
gaps.why: CONNACK offset 2, bit 0 (sessionPresent). If it were 1, the broker has resurrected subscriptions from a previous connection — subscriptions this run never created and whose granted QoS values it never saw. That is neither confirmed (we did not observe the grant) nor presumed (we did not request it): it is asserted-by-peer over persisted state. §5 has confirmed and presumed only.
gaps.proposedFix:
"effects": { "restore": { "from":"store.mqtt.subscriptions", "to":"session.subscriptions",
                          "when":"capture.sessionPresent == 1", "confidence":"peer-asserted" },
             "clear":   { "scope":"session.subscriptions", "when":"capture.sessionPresent == 0" } }
plus "peer-asserted" as a third confidence tier below "confirmed".

gaps.what: No occurrence bound per state or per session.
gaps.why: CONNECT is legal EXACTLY ONCE per TCP connection; a second one is a protocol violation the broker must answer by closing. §5's `conflicts` is pairwise across DIFFERENT messages and cannot express self-occurrence. Related: `requires:["login"]` has no declared scope (run / session / store), so on reconnect a satisfied `requires` may silently carry over and authorise a SUBSCRIBE on a fresh un-CONNECTed socket.
gaps.proposedFix: "maxPerSession": 1 on the message, and make `requires` scope explicit: "requires": [ { "message":"mqttConnect", "scope":"session" } ] — with `session` invalidated on any transition to tcpClosed.

gaps.what: No side effect attached to ABNORMAL state exit.
gaps.why: The Will message (CONNECT offsets 32..125) is published by the broker if and only if the connection ends WITHOUT a DISCONNECT. It is the one piece of protocol state whose outcome depends on HOW a state was exited rather than on any message sent. §5's `effects` attach to a message SUCCEEDING; abnormal termination is precisely the case where no message was sent.
gaps.proposedFix: On the state: "onAbnormalExit": { "presume": { "dev.mqtt.willPublished": true, "dev.mqtt.lastWillTopic":"inputs.willTopic" }, "confidence":"likely" }, with abnormal defined as any exit not via a declared `graceful` transition (DISCONNECT).

gaps.what: `bits` semantics are undefined: fill order, byte-multiple requirement, multi-byte endianness.
gaps.why: CONNECT offset 10 must be 0xce = userName(1) password(1) willRetain(0) willQoS(01) willFlag(1) cleanSession(1) reserved(0), MSB-first. §3 shows {"bits":[{"n":1},{"n":3},{"n":4}]} without stating fill direction. LSB-first would emit 0x73 — a completely different, still-syntactically-valid packet. Silent 50/50.
gaps.proposedFix: Specify: `bits` fills MSB-first within each byte; the sum of all `n` MUST be a multiple of 8 (validate-time error otherwise); a group spanning >1 byte fills bytes in wire order. Add optional "order":"msb|lsb" defaulting to msb for protocols that differ.

gaps.what: Spec self-contradiction: §2 lists `mqtt` as a sugar layer, but §7 forbids protocol-specific code paths — and §6 defines a converter-only expression language that §3's own example violates.
gaps.why: §2 says `mqtt` is "sugar — expands to bytes + a transport intent" but never says what it expands TO. If it encodes the varint, the framing and the length-prefixed strings, then it IS the MQTT-specific code path §7 says means "the grammar has failed". Testing against it would fake a pass, so I built everything on `bytes`. Separately: §6 declares a pipeline language `a | f(b)` with a CLOSED converter set containing no arithmetic and no comparison, yet §3's decode example writes "capture.byteCount / 2" and §5 writes "capture.status == 200" and "session.token != ''". Infix arithmetic and comparison therefore exist de facto and are wholly unspecified — and my varint workaround depends on % / + and >=, so under a STRICT reading of §6 even the cheat is inexpressible.
gaps.proposedFix: Two statements. (1) Delete `mqtt` (and `coap`, `modbus`, `snmp`, `dns`) from §2's layer table, or redefine each as a NAMED, PUBLISHED macro that expands to the documented `bytes` fields and nothing else — with the expansion checked in by a test asserting macro output == hand-written bytes output. (2) Extend §6 with an explicit infix grammar and its precedence/type rules: arithmetic + - * / %, comparison == != < <= > >=, boolean && || !, all over Int, with the same validate-time kind checking the converters already have. Otherwise every existing example in the spec is illegal under its own §6.
